issues.legal_issue: A magistrate presiding over a criminal trial must not enter the arena by filing an affidavit opposing an accused person's transfer application.
material_facts: An accused person whose criminal case was pending before a magistrate sought transfer of the case.
The magistrate himself filed an affidavit on behalf of the administration opposing transfer.
The affidavit addressed the accused person's allegations and advanced an argument that could be made by the complainant at trial.
issues.conclusion: The magistrate's action in making the affidavit and opposing the transfer application was wholly improper.
issues.legal_principle: A judge must remain impartial and must not act as a partisan for the administration or prosecution. In criminal trials, the magistrate must remain fearless, impartial and objective; a magistrate's partisan opposition to an accused person's transfer application puts the essential attributes of a fair trial in jeopardy. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: criminal_trial_pending and accused_sought_transfer and trial_magistrate_filed_opposition_affidavit and affidavit_advanced_prosecution_argument

predicates.criminal_trial_pending: A criminal trial was pending before the magistrate.
predicates.accused_sought_transfer: An accused person asked for the criminal case to be transferred.
predicates.trial_magistrate_filed_opposition_affida: The magistrate trying the case filed an affidavit opposing the accused person's transfer request.
predicates.affidavit_advanced_prosecution_argument: The magistrate's affidavit advanced an argument that could be made by the prosecution at trial.

issues.definition: When a criminal trial is pending, an accused seeks transfer, and the trial magistrate files an opposing affidavit advancing a prosecution argument, the magistrate's affidavit is wholly improper.

issues.legal_issue: A criminal case should be transferred when the trial magistrate's partisan opposition to an accused person's transfer application jeopardizes the fairness of the trial.
material_facts: An accused person applied to transfer a criminal case pending before the magistrate.
The magistrate filed an affidavit opposing transfer on behalf of the administration and advanced a position on an issue relevant to the accused person's defence.
The court concluded that the magistrate had entered the arena and that the essential attributes of a fair and impartial trial were in jeopardy.
issues.conclusion: The case should be transferred to a court of competent jurisdiction in the interests of justice, without deciding the merits of the accused person's other contentions.
issues.legal_principle: A transfer is expedient in the interests of justice where the conduct of the magistrate presiding over a criminal trial puts the fairness and impartiality of that trial in jeopardy. The judgment relies on the elementary principle that judges must not enter the arena and must remain impartial; it cites no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this ruling.

rule.if: criminal_case_transfer_petition and accused_sought_transfer and trial_magistrate_filed_opposition_affidavit and affidavit_put_fair_trial_in_jeopardy

predicates.criminal_case_transfer_petition: A petition sought transfer of a pending criminal case.
predicates.accused_sought_transfer: An accused person asked for the criminal case to be transferred.
predicates.trial_magistrate_filed_opposition_affida: The magistrate trying the case filed an affidavit opposing the transfer request.
predicates.affidavit_put_fair_trial_in_jeopardy: The magistrate's affidavit took a partisan position that placed the fairness and impartiality of the trial in jeopardy.

issues.definition: When a criminal case is the subject of a transfer petition and the trial magistrate's opposing affidavit jeopardizes a fair trial, transfer is required in the interests of justice.

issues.legal_issue: A criminal case may be transferred as a whole without separately determining whether the other accused persons agree when the transfer is justified by circumstances centred on the principal accused and the other accused are alleged to have acted as that person's agents.
material_facts: The transfer application was made by one accused person, who was alleged to be the principal accused.
The complaint alleged that the other accused persons were involved as agents and representatives of the principal accused.
The court ordered transfer of the case and did not consider whether the other accused persons agreed to the transfer.
issues.conclusion: The court transferred the case against all the accused persons without separately determining whether the other accused persons agreed to the transfer.
issues.legal_principle: In the unusual circumstances of this case, where the other accused were alleged to be involved only as agents and representatives of the principal accused, the court considered it unnecessary to determine whether they agreed to transfer. The judgment cites no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this aspect of its decision.

predicates.criminal_case_transfer_petition: A petition sought transfer of a pending criminal case.
predicates.transfer_justified_by_circumstances_conc: The circumstances justifying transfer concerned the accused person alleged to be the principal accused.
predicates.other_accused_alleged_to_be_principal_ac: The complaint alleged that the other accused persons were involved only as agents or representatives of the principal accused.

issues.definition: When transfer is justified by circumstances concerning the principal accused and the other accused are alleged to be that person's agents, the entire case may be transferred without a separate inquiry into their consent.
